questions.prompt: What does the acronym SONAR stand for?
hints: The first two letters come from the word sound.
It uses reflected underwater sound to find objects.

questions.prompt: What does the acronym RADAR stand for?
hints: It replaced the older term 'radio location'.
It bounces radio waves off objects.

questions.prompt: On a ship, which side is port and which is starboard?
questions.answer: Port is the left side and starboard is the right side, facing forward
hints: Both are named facing the bow.
Port is the shorter word of the two, and it is the shorter crossing.

questions.prompt: What are the front and rear of a ship called?
questions.answer: The front is the bow and the rear is the stern
hints: The rear one also names the direction of movement when going backwards.
The forward one takes the spray.

questions.prompt: Which submarine was the world's first nuclear-powered submarine, and in what year did she go to sea?
hints: She shares her name with Captain Nemo's vessel.
The year is mid-1950s, same decade as the first nuclear-powered carrier.

questions.prompt: Which ship was the first nuclear-powered aircraft carrier?
hints: She shares a name with a famous starship.
Her hull number is CVN-65.

questions.prompt: Where is the United States Naval Academy located, and in what year was it founded?
hints: The city is also the capital of its state.
The decade is the 1840s.

questions.prompt: One knot equals how many nautical miles per hour, and how many kilometres per hour?
questions.answer: One nautical mile per hour, about 1.852 kilometres per hour
hints: A knot is a speed, never a distance.
One nautical mile is 1,852 metres.

questions.prompt: In Navy signal flags and voice procedure, what does 'Bravo Zulu' mean?
questions.answer: Well done, or a job well done
hints: It is usually abbreviated to two letters.
It is praise, not a warning.

questions.prompt: On what date is the United States Navy's birthday observed?
hints: It marks the founding of the Continental Navy.
The Marine Corps birthday is about a month later, in November.

questions.prompt: On what date is the United States Marine Corps birthday?
hints: It falls in November, shortly after the Navy's October birthday.
The year is the same as the Navy's founding year.

questions.prompt: What is the United States Navy's official song?
hints: It is played at football games and at commissioning.
The title mentions a raising of anchors.

questions.prompt: What is the lowest commissioned officer rank in the United States Navy?
hints: It sits just above a chief warrant officer and below lieutenant junior grade.
A one-stripe gold shoulder board or collar device marks it.

questions.prompt: The distress call 'mayday' comes from which language and phrase?
questions.answer: French, from 'm'aider' (short for venez m'aider, 'come help me')
hints: It is a Romance language.
The phrase means 'help me'.

questions.prompt: Where does the United States Navy conduct enlisted recruit training?
questions.answer: Recruit Training Command, Great Lakes, Illinois
hints: It is on a lake, not an ocean.
It is the Navy's only enlisted boot camp.

questions.prompt: What does the order 'all hands' refer to?
questions.answer: The entire crew of the ship
hints: It is a general announcement, not a station.
It leaves nobody out.
